style_when: the news is structural and abstract — a stack reordered, a layer added, a flow rerouted — and there is no literal object that carries it, so the idea is stated as a small physical assembly of recognisable parts rather than as bare shapes
prompt: A split-screen clay assembly on a loading bay concrete floor. Left half: a brushed-steel track carries an unmarked brown cardboard parcel into a carrier dock slot with a safety-yellow modular housing; right half: the same parcel passes through a hinged graphite steel boundary gate into a bone-white shipper dock module with polymer side panels. One directional key light rakes from the left across matte surfaces, casting long shadows. Split-screen diptych, extreme asymmetry, muted graphite, safety yellow, bone white.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, numbers
rationale: Clay_render turns the rate card's boundary into a small mechanical assembly—a parcel crossing between modular dock slots—making the ownership switch legible without photographic literalism. The split-screen contrasts carrier Scope 3 with shipper Scope 1.
cue: The rate card is a boundary
subject: a cardboard parcel crossing a hinged boundary gate between two modular delivery docks
core_thesis: A parcel rate card rising 5.9% pushes shippers to run the last mile themselves, and ownership—not mileage—decides whether a delivery's fuel is the shipper's own Scope 1 or a carrier's Scope 3, so the cheaper mile and the reported mile can move in opposite directions.
core_conflict: Cost-driven insourcing of last-mile delivery shifts carbon emissions from a carrier's Scope 3 to a shipper's Scope 1, making the cheaper operational mile a potentially worse reported carbon line.
composition: split-screen diptych with left-right scenario contrast

title: Your 5.9% Hike Moves Your Carbon

review.depicts: A split-frame matte render: on the left a brown cardboard box sits on a metal rail protruding from a mustard-yellow padded rectangular dock with a square opening, and on the right a similar box sits on a dark platform at the open hinged mesh gate of a cream-white block structure with translucent panel walls, both on a grey concrete floor.
review.reason: The parcel crossing a hinged gate between two docks is the article's own protagonist at its own mechanism — the ownership boundary that decides Scope 1 versus Scope 3 — though nothing in the frame itself signals rates, carbon or the 5.9% hike.
